extracted.intended_audience: Boys & Girls Clubs of Northwest San Diego staff, volunteers, leadership, and member organizations (youth-serving program administrators)
extracted.subtask_description: Organizational safety and child-protection policies for a regional Boys & Girls Clubs network covering abuse prevention, one-to-one interactions, virtual session privacy, supervision, screening/onboarding, drug-free workplace, facilities, restroom/locker-room practices, and related procedures. Intended to provide minimum standards, required trainings, and operational guidance for staff/volunteers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Membership Safety Requirements / Adoption and Training
rubrics_metrics.description: All member organizations are required to adopt and adhere to safety policies that protect youth, and all staff and volunteers must be trained on these policies annually.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BGCA will review and approve minimum safety policies authored by CSQA for adoption by all Clubs; Clubs may supplement with operational detail specific to each site. Upon adoption and annually thereafter National Council reviews policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Child Abuse Prevention Policy (zero-tolerance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Priority is physical and emotional safety; BGCA maintains a zero-tolerance policy for child abuse. Policies/procedures exist for members, employees, volunteers, visitors or victims to report suspicion or allegation of abuse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines one-to-one contact prohibition and lists allowed exceptions (licensed professionals).

rubrics_metrics.name: One-to-One Contact Prohibition (definition and scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prohibits isolated one-to-one interaction between Club participants and staff or volunteers, including board members, at the Club, in vehicles, by phone, text, social media or any other means.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions only for approved medical or counseling services by licensed professionals per professional guidelines. All staff and volunteers, including minors, are prohibited from meeting Club participants outside Club-sponsored activities except if participant is a child/sibling of staff/volunteer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Child Abuse and Sexual Misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Child abuse is when an adult or another child causes serious emotional or physical harm through action or inaction. Sexual abuse/misconduct examples include sexual activity with minors, sexual activity with legally incompetent persons, physical sexual violence, unwanted sexual touching, and inappropriate sexualized communications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides non-exhaustive examples (rape, molestation, unwanted touching, sexual comments, electronic communications).

rubrics_metrics.name: Grooming Behavior Definition and Examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Grooming is building an emotional connection with a child to gain trust for sexual abuse/exploitation/trafficking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include targeting specific youth for special attention/gifts, isolating youth from family/friends, gradually crossing physical boundaries (long hugs, lap sitting), and facilitating isolated interactions like sleepovers or private trips.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandated Reporting Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Every staff member or volunteer who becomes aware of or suspects child abuse or neglect must immediately report to Club leadership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Club leadership must report immediately to appropriate authorities per state laws and to BGCA within 24 hours via the critical incident system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required Trainings (pre-service and annual)
rubrics_metrics.description: Before providing services and annually thereafter, staff/volunteers with direct repetitive contact must complete BGCA-approved trainings: child abuse prevention, mandated reporting, grooming prevention, and the organization's safety policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additionally, annually review all organizational policies including safety policies; trainings referenced include 'Foundations: Preventing Abuse in Youth-Serving Organizations' and 'Duty to Report: Mandated Reporter'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate vs Inappropriate Physical Interactions
rubrics_metrics.description: Staff/volunteers must maintain appropriate physical contact; list of appropriate interactions (side hugs, handshakes, high-fives, holding hands for escorting young children) and inappropriate interactions (full-frontal hugs/kisses, showing affection in isolated area, wrestling/piggyback rides, tickling, lap sitting, allowing youth to cling to adult).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are examples, not exhaustive; staff must avoid listed inappropriate behaviors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate vs Inappropriate Verbal Interactions
rubrics_metrics.description: Staff/volunteers must maintain appropriate verbal interactions; appropriate examples (positive reinforcement, child-appropriate jokes, encouragement, praise) and inappropriate examples (name calling, inappropriate adult jokes, discussing sexual encounters/personal issues, secrets, profanity, derogatory remarks, harsh frightening language).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These lists are illustrative; staff must avoid verbal conduct that may frighten, threaten, humiliate or sexualize youth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abuse and Safety Resources Communication
rubrics_metrics.description: BGCA-approved collateral (ethics hotline, crisis text-line, safety helpline) must be prominently displayed and safety policies shared with parents/guardians upon youth membership application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides links to mandated reporter training resources and notes trainings are housed on Spillett Leadership University.

rubrics_metrics.name: One-To-One Interactions Policy (prohibitions and basic rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prohibits one-to-one interactions between Youth Members and Applicable Adults that are not observable and interruptible; ensure meetings/communications are never private; in-person meetings must be where others present; never initiate private contact; never transport one member alone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions may be documented for licensed medical/counseling professionals or emergencies; exceptions must be communicated to Club leadership in advance if possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: One-To-One Interaction Policy Guidance (private vs public contact)
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines private contact/communication (between one youth and one adult in secluded area or without others' knowledge) with examples, and public contact/communication (between at least three individuals or meetings in plain sight) with examples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Private places examples: vehicles, rooms without visibility, private homes, hotel rooms. Public examples: meetings in plain sight, group electronic communications, public transportation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observable and Interruptible Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: One-to-one interactions between a Youth Member and an Applicable Adult (not the minor's guardian) must be observable and interruptible by another adult unless meeting with mental/health care professional or under emergency circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observable means visible/open; interruptible means another adult can enter or observe the interaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meeting Location and Conduct Rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Meetings may only occur if another adult is present and interactions can be easily observed/interrupted; room door must remain unlocked and open; meetings must not be conducted in hotel rooms or overnight lodging during travel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If available, use rooms with windows and keep blinds/curtains open; legal guardians must be allowed to observe in certain individual training/lesson contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meetings with Mental Health Care Professionals / Health Care Providers
rubrics_metrics.description: Closed-door meetings may be permitted to protect patient privacy if door remains unlocked, another adult is present at facility and advised, written guardian consent obtained in advance and provided to organization, and health care providers also have another adult in the room.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document guardian consent and maintain observability/interruptibility within facility constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individual Training Sessions for Youth Athletes
rubrics_metrics.description: Individual training sessions outside regular training/practice are permitted only if observable and interruptible by another adult; legal guardians must be allowed to observe; parents cannot drop off and leave children unattended when only one adult present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Staff/volunteer coaches must require another adult present even if that adult is the minor's parent or childcare provider.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individual Lessons and Youth Arts Academy Rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Individual lessons may occur as closed-door sessions if they are observable and interruptible, in rooms with windows and unlocked doors; another adult should be present at facility and guardians allowed to observe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain ability for observation/interruptibility and allow guardian presence/observation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transportation Safety Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Only approved BGCNWSD drivers or approved transportation companies may transport youth; youth should never be transported in a one-to-one situation unless emergency; at least one other Applicable Adult should be present when one youth is transported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes Club or leased vehicles; emergency exceptions documented and reported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social Media and Electronic Communications — Professional Content
rubrics_metrics.description: All electronic communication from Applicable Adults to youth must be professional in nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid personal, sexual, or otherwise inappropriate content; use organization-approved communication channels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social Media and Electronic Communications — Open and Transparent
rubrics_metrics.description: If an Applicable Adult communicates electronically with a Youth Member, the youth's legal guardian must be copied; if youth initiates privately, the adult must copy guardian on responses; group communications must include another adult.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures transparency and avoids private one-on-one electronic contacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requests to Discontinue Electronic Contact
rubrics_metrics.description: Legal guardians may request in writing that their child not be contacted through any form of electronic communication by the Organization or Applicable Adults.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organization will abide unless an emergency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hours of Electronic Communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Electronic communications to Youth Members must only be sent between 8:00 a.m. and 8:00 p.m., unless emergency or during program/team travel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limits contact to reasonable hours to protect youth privacy/safety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibited Electronic Communication Practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicable Adults may not maintain private social media connections with unrelated Youth Members, accept new personal page requests from Youth Members, or send private/direct messages via social media; existing social media connections with youth must be discontinued (exceptions: fan pages/celebrity contacts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Youth may follow the organization's official social accounts; private instant messaging is prohibited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Live Video Meetings Safety Criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: One-to-one video meetings (FaceTime/Zoom/etc.) are allowed only if observable and interruptible: include at least two Applicable Adults on the call OR a guardian checks in at onset; meetings must be scheduled and calendared by employees; Applicable Adults must notify employees of scheduling needs and must initiate (youth cannot initiate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Video meetings should be observable, calendared by BGCNWSD employees, and have guardian or second-adult presence as described.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting Violations and Disciplinary Action
rubrics_metrics.description: Staff must immediately inform supervisors if an Applicable Adult violates the one-to-one policy; organization will take appropriate disciplinary action up to termination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Immediate reporting and follow-up procedures should be followed to ensure safety and compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exception Handling and Monitoring for One-on-One Situations
rubrics_metrics.description: Exceptions (licensed professionals, emergencies) may be made but must be disclosed to leadership, have monitoring procedures, time limits, clear sightlines, documentation of interaction, and disclosure to another staff member before engaging when possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Club shall have policies in place to monitor exceptions including regular check-ins, documentation, and environmental controls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Virtual One-To-One Interactions Privacy Notice — Scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines virtual one-to-one interactions (video conferencing, texting, email, social media) and describes how personal information may be collected, saved, used or disclosed when participating in virtual sessions (e.g., Zoom).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice applies to tutoring, mentoring, instructional lessons conducted virtually and explains recordings, data collection, and parental consent rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information Collected for Virtual Sessions
rubrics_metrics.description: May collect participants' first/last names, usernames, phone numbers, email addresses, and, with parental consent, recordings of sessions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collection is for registration, scheduling, participation tracking and program quality; recordings retained only as needed for educational purposes; requests for deletion honored via contact email.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording Policy for Virtual Sessions
rubrics_metrics.description: Organizations may record virtual one-to-one interactions with consent; recordings available only to child/guardian and staff and kept only as long as needed for educational access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approved volunteers/organizations are strictly prohibited from collecting or storing recordings of sessions; parents may request deletion at any time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and Disclosure of Virtual Session Information
rubrics_metrics.description: Information is used to register participants, schedule sessions, track participation, assist lesson delivery, and ensure program quality. Information will not be shared except when necessary to protect rights/safety, to comply with legal obligations, to defend legal claims, or as described in the notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For other uses, organization will notify and obtain consent as necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approved Volunteers' Access to Virtual Session Data
rubrics_metrics.description: Approved volunteers/organizations participating in virtual sessions may have access to participant information necessary to provide services (e.g., volunteer tutor will learn name/contact info).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Volunteers are prohibited from collecting, accessing, or storing session recordings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third-Party Platform (Zoom) Data Practices Notice
rubrics_metrics.description: When using Zoom, Zoom may collect basic info (name, username, email, phone, location, cookies/browser data); organization settings maximize protections but the organization does not control Zoom practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parents/guardians should be aware of Zoom's independent data practices; organization configures settings to optimize privacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Children Under 13 — Parental Consent and Rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Children under 13 may only participate in virtual one-to-one sessions with parental consent; parents may access, change, delete their child's personal information or withdraw consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organization provides contact methods to exercise these rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgement and Consent for Virtual Participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Signing the Acknowledgement and Consent indicates guardian has read the Privacy Notice, consents to information use as described, consents to participation and consent to recording.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Written consent form fields for participant/guardian name and signature are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supervision and Facilities — Continuous Supervision Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: All Club activities and program spaces must be under continuous supervision by sight or sound (for restroom) by an appropriate adult (18 or over).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Staff must abide by one-to-one prohibition, disciplinary policies, maintain proper supervision ratios, be trained, supervise youth staff/volunteers, report supervision issues/accidents/critical incidents, and avoid electronic device use while supervising except for Club purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restroom Usage Policy (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: There will be either designated adult restrooms or procedures to ensure adults and minors never utilize a restroom at the same time; use single-user restrooms or multi-user restrooms with single lockable stalls.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On field trips, minimum of three youth escorted by one staff who waits outside main restroom entrance; staff must monitor restrooms per schedule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restroom Monitoring Practices and Best Practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Restrooms shall be regularly monitored via walk-throughs and inspections; implement procedures to limit number of children using restrooms at once, prohibit younger children and teens sharing, position staff near entries to maintain auditory supervision, and design spaces to eliminate outer doors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Staff observing unacceptable restroom conditions must notify leadership and document incidents per incident reporting policy; prohibit audio/visual devices in restrooms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entrance and Exit Control for Facilities
rubrics_metrics.description: All facility entries/exits shall be controlled and monitored by paid adult staff (18 or over) during operational hours with a system to track everyone in facility; exit doors shall have audible alarms; only designated adults have keys/badges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employees supervising scheduled activities are responsible for security of program space.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facility Condition and Maintenance
rubrics_metrics.description: Program spaces must have clear lines of visibility, be monitored by adult staff, lock unused areas, be well-lit, clean, free of hazards, and repair damages in reasonable time; damages posing imminent risk must be repaired immediately or facility closed as determined by leadership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critical incidents arising from facility damage must be reported to appropriate authorities as a critical incident.

rubrics_metrics.name: Food and Drink Safety Compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Any distribution, preparation, or consumption of food/drink must comply with applicable food sanitation and public health codes; required health inspection certificates posted if food prepared on site; dangerous utensils stored securely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow local health department requirements; ensure safe storage and posting of certificates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staff-to-Member Ratios (program-specific minimums)
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain reasonable supervision ratios based on program type (After School, Instructional classes, Group Clubs, Sports Teams, Day Camps, Day Field Trips, Overnight Trips, Swimming).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides tabulated minimum applicable adults and maximum youth counts (e.g., After School 1:20; Instructional 1:20; Day Camps 1:15; Overnight Trips 1:8; Swimming: 1 lifeguard per 25 swimmers and 1 spotter per 10 swimmers). Ratios based on experience and standards; staff must maintain ratios.

rubrics_metrics.name: Screening and Onboarding — Background Checks (minimum elements)
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct criminal background checks of employees (including minors), board volunteers, standing committee members, and volunteers with direct repetitive contact. Background check shall at minimum verify identity/SSN, provide national Sex Offender Registry search, provide comprehensive national and local criminal searches, and include any additional checks required by policies/funding/licensing or jurisdiction (e.g., motor vehicle records, child abuse registry, credit checks).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Checks conducted prior to employment and at regular intervals not to exceed 12 months; findings considered in hiring/volunteer decisions; refusal/false statement/sex offender registration/serious convictions disqualify.

rubrics_metrics.name: Screening Disqualifying Convictions / Considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Organization will not employ or engage individuals who refuse consent, falsify background check statements, are registered or required to register on sex offender registry, or have convictions for serious offenses (murder, child abuse, domestic violence, abduction/trafficking, rape/sexual assault, arson, weapons, physical assault/battery, recent drug offenses, crimes against children including child pornography).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Background check findings considered for employment decisions; specifics include drug possession/use/distribution in last five years and misdemeanors/felonies against children.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drug Screening in Hiring
rubrics_metrics.description: All employment applicants are screened for illegal drugs prior to employment and follow the organization's drug-screening process in accordance with Drug-Free Workplace Policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Drug-Free Workplace section for details and possible corrective measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interviewing Practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct in-person behavioral-based interviews with every candidate for employment or program volunteer service; candidates may go through various interview stages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Behavioral interviewing to assess suitability for roles with youth contact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference Checks Policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct reference checks on candidates with direct repetitive contact with youth; obtain rehire/eligibility info from prior Boys & Girls Clubs employers before extending offers; provide reference materials when requested by other member organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference checks are part of assessing prior behavior and suitability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staff and Volunteer Onboarding Content
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon offer, new staff receive and confirm receipt of handbook articulating conditions of employment, benefits, rights/responsibilities, club safety policies, and other employment-related info. Before working with members, staff/volunteers receive orientation covering mission/goals/policies, job descriptions/performance standards, participant needs/characteristics, personnel expectations, operational policies (safety, supervision, transportation, emergency), and completion of required Child Abuse Prevention Trainings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Orientation must occur prior to working with members; ongoing training provided throughout year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hiring Process Completion Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: All new hires must successfully complete required pre-employment steps prior to first day (drug screening, background checks, fingerprinting). Organization reserves right to alter hiring practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures consistent completion of safety-related onboarding before exposure to youth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drug and Alcohol-Free Workplace Policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Organization is committed to a drug-and alcohol-free workplace per Federal and California law. Employees/volunteers prohibited from reporting to work or working under influence; prohibited from using alcohol/illegal/unauthorized drugs at work or representing the organization (with limited approved event exceptions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definition includes illegal drugs, abused prescription/OTC drugs; employees must notify supervisor/HR within five days of any drug/alcohol-related conviction; organization may impose corrective measures including termination or require rehabilitation participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prescription and Legal Drug Use Rules
rubrics_metrics.description: No prescription drug may be brought on premises by anyone except the person prescribed; legal drugs used only as prescribed/manufacturer instructions. Employees whose legal drug use may affect safety/performance must notify supervisor/HR and may need accommodation or leave.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If healthcare provider concludes employee cannot perform essential functions safely even with accommodation, leave may be required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of Drug/Alcohol Convictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Employees must notify their supervisor, Club leadership and Chief Human Resources Officer within five days of any conviction of a drug/alcohol-related crime.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organization may take actions within 30 days of notice, including termination or requiring approved rehabilitation programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restroom Procedures and Site-Specific Practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Site-specific restroom procedures (e.g., Griset, Polster, Harper, La Colonia, Carmel Valley Montessori) include closing/locking exterior restroom doors when adults use restrooms, posting signs/cones to indicate adult usage, youth-only hours, adult-only restrooms, and staff monitoring practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Field trips follow 'rule of three' (2 youth + 1 adult or 1 staff with 2 youth); staff should attempt to clear public restrooms before youth use; position staff at entries or partially open doors to supervise; document incidents and conduct sweeps before closing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accommodations for Gender Nonconforming Youth
rubrics_metrics.description: Allow youth, staff, volunteers, and other adults to utilize restroom facilities consistent with their gender identity, gender expression, and transgender status; Club Manager shall meet with youth and guardians to plan restroom access and confirm comfort.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Youth may opt for privacy by shutting exterior door and using 'Occupied' sign; ensure privacy and safety consistent with policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Field Trip and Public Restroom Policy
rubrics_metrics.description: On field trips/public restrooms, youth shall never enter a restroom alone unless it's an empty single-user restroom (staff should remain by door). Use rule of three, position staff near entries, conduct staff sweeps and assess facility before youth use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Staff/volunteers will walk in restroom facilities first and position themselves to avoid 1:1 situations; document and report incidents.

rubrics_metrics.name: General Restroom Use Guidelines and Best Practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Limit mixed age groups, limit number of youths using restrooms at once, display codes of conduct, enforce rules, prohibit recording devices, document incidents, position staff near entrances, conduct sweeps, implement inspection logs, maintain repairs, sanitize regularly, and provide training on restroom policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement a system for reporting restroom conditions and maintenance needs; orientation and training should cover these guidelines during new hire and ongoing training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Locker Room Policy — Purpose and Definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Locker room policy designed to maintain personal privacy and increase safety, prevent bullying/sexual misconduct/fighting/vandalism; locker room defined to include showers, changing area, and single-stall restrooms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy enhanced to comply with USA Swimming Safe Sport MAPP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Locker Room — Requirement to Use Designated Changing Areas
rubrics_metrics.description: Designated locker room or changing area must be used when any youth/adult changes into or out of a swimsuit; deck changing is prohibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of single-stall restrooms as changing rooms permitted upon request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Locker Room — Youth Only Times and Adult Access
rubrics_metrics.description: Locker rooms/changing areas may be designated Youth Only during specified times; during Youth Only hours, adults directed to Adult Only restrooms and exterior locker room doors should remain open if privacy can be maintained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Youth Only times are posted; adults discouraged from entering unless same-sex guardian assisting own child and must notify staff in advance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Locker Room — Single-Stall Restroom Use
rubrics_metrics.description: Single-stall restrooms within locker rooms shall be occupied by only one person at a time; exceptions for young children requiring assistance by their own legal guardian or qualified staff where the stall remains unlocked and interaction observable/interruptible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain documentation of guardian authorization when staff assist minors and follow observable/interruptible rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Locker Room — Legal Guardians and Staff Presence
rubrics_metrics.description: Legal guardians are discouraged from entering locker rooms/changing areas; if they do to assist their child it must be a same-sex guardian and they should notify staff in advance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If qualified person other than guardian assists, one-on-one interaction should be observable and interruptible; use rule of three for assistance when feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Locker Room — One-on-One Interaction Prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: Adults other than legal guardians are never permitted to be exclusively alone with a minor in locker rooms or changing areas except in emergencies; if help is required from qualified person other than guardian, interaction must be observable/interruptible and documented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For young children needing help with swimwear, ensure at least two staff are present to avoid 1:1 and have signed acknowledgement from guardian authorizing staff assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Locker Room — Monitoring Methods and Sweeps
rubrics_metrics.description: Locker rooms/changing areas are regularly and randomly monitored via sweeps before athletes arrive, posting staff outside during use, leaving doors open when privacy allows, and occasional gender-matched sweeps (women checking female locker rooms, men checking male locker rooms).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitoring balanced with privacy considerations; staff should check on youths who do not return in timely fashion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Locker Room — Use of Recording Devices Prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: Cell phones, still cameras, video cameras and any device with recording capabilities (including voice recording) are strictly prohibited in locker rooms and changing areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict prohibition as recording devices increase risk for misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Locker Room — Additional Staff Guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Limit mixed youth age groups in locker rooms, accommodate gender identity, make single-stall restroom available as changing room, display and enforce codes of conduct, document incidents, conduct sweeps before closing, implement inspection schedules and logging, report maintenance needs, keep facilities in repair and sanitized, and provide training during hire and throughout the year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Same practices as restrooms applied to locker rooms with emphasis on privacy and safety.
